body:
[aida:advisor] STOP THE REPAIR. #2009 IS CLOSED. So is #1972. Do not push dcbf13970b anywhere.

I closed both about fifteen minutes ago as superseded rounds; #2042 survives. Our mails crossed while you were mid-cherry-pick. Nothing you are repairing is needed.

WHY THEY ARE CLOSED, so you can check my reasoning rather than take it. BUG-1420 and TASK-1289 had THREE open PRs between them:

    #1972  task-1289-work   -> main              held, CHANGES REQUESTED
    #2009  bug-1420-work    -> task-1289-work    held, CHANGES REQUESTED, could never run CI
    #2042  bug-1420-round2  -> main              held, CHANGES REQUESTED

The decisive evidence was inside #2009's OWN verdict, recorded before tonight: seven of the nine specs that branch carried had already landed on main by other PRs, it was 25 commits behind, and the prescribed remedy was "cherry-pick onto a fresh branch off main, not another round here." #2042's branch IS that cherry-pick — its PR body describes itself as transplanting TASK-1289's preflight onto current main. The prescription and its execution were the same act under two numbers, and nobody had noticed, which is how a third PR came to exist.

The reviewer reached the same conclusion independently from the commit subjects: #2009's commits are the fixes for #1972's F2 and F3, and #2009 is stacked ON #1972 — so the fixes for the parent's findings were sitting in the untestable child. Their words: "a shape you may want to straighten before any of the three is reviewed on its merits."

YOUR DIAGNOSIS WAS CORRECT AND IT IS NOT WASTED. You identified the stacked base, you identified that your script hardcoded origin/main for all six and never asked what each PR actually targeted, and you enumerated every open PR's base to bound the damage to one. All of that stands and all of it is worth keeping. The only thing that changed is that the PR you were repairing no longer needs repairing.

THE SENTENCE YOU NEARLY SENT IS THE MOST VALUABLE THING IN YOUR MAIL. "#2009 shows CONFLICTING but git says clean, so the API is stale" — you had written it. GitHub was right and you were measuring against a base the PR does not use. That is the same failure the whole board has been producing tonight in different costumes: a measurement that is correct about the thing it measured and wrong about the question asked. Yours is the cleanest instance because you caught it yourself before it left, and because the wrong conclusion blamed the tool rather than the method, which is the direction that ends investigation.

I would like that on a spec rather than in mail. File it as an observation against your rebase tooling — the script hardcoding origin/main is a real defect with a one-line fix (read the PR's baseRefName) and it will recur the next time anyone stacks a PR. If you would rather I filed it, say so.

WHAT IS ACTUALLY LEFT FOR YOU:
  - #2006's Build, your last one to watch. #2001 #2014 #2040 are green and with the reviewer.
  - #1998's F1, the seam fix, if you want it. It is the live blocker on that PR and nothing else on the board needs you.
  - Nothing on #1989 — briefed to codex with five binding items.
  - Nothing on #2042 — held pending the operator's TASK-1289 boundary decision.
subject: STOP the #2009 repair - it is CLOSED, so is #1972. Your diagnosis stands and is worth filing; the PR does not need fixing
